title: fix(core): an import lookup naming a detail resolves within the row's own master
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DFWmDYdUPFhME7Z7Ky3ySCZ)_

Fixes #33523
Area-lease pilot #33059, area A3.

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — widening: a row whose master identifies one of several same-named details now resolves it, where it was refused `reference_ambiguous`; `@objectstack/core` gains the export `referenceScopeSources`, the types `ReferenceMaster` / `ReferenceScopeSource`, and optional parameters on `RefResolver`, `coerceFieldValue`, `coerceRow`, `CoerceContext` and `ExportFieldMeta`. Narrowing: a row that names a master and a detail only another master carries is refused `reference_not_found`, where that detail was linked across masters; and a caller who cannot read the target's master field (or a `dependsOn` `param` field) is refused `reference_not_found` for a scoped lookup cell that the unscoped lookup resolved, because the scope puts that field into the caller's own filter and a filter on a field the caller cannot read is refused.
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: `content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx` gains "A lookup cell is resolved within the row's own master"; `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md` names the scoping under `master_detail`.

## 维护者速读

- What changed: a data import resolving a lookup cell now searches only within the master record the same row sets, when the target is that master's detail (`master_detail`) or the field declares `dependsOn`.
- Why: with two contracts each carrying an "Advance 30%" billing step, an invoice import row failed with `reference_ambiguous` although its own contract picks one; the record form's picker already narrows by contract (measured by HotCRM's invoice import template).
- Risk and rollback: two answers narrow. A row naming contract B and a step that only contract A has used to link A's step; it now fails `reference_not_found`. A caller who cannot read the step's contract field now gets `reference_not_found` for a step the row scopes by contract, even when its name is unique. Remedy for both: correct the master cell, or leave the master column out and set it in a second update. Rollback is a revert of this PR; no data migration.
- Look first: `referenceScopeSources` and the two-pass `coerceRow` in `packages/core/src/utils/import-coerce.ts`; the `where` merge and cache key in `packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts`; the new `import-runner-reference-master-scope.test.ts`.
- Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core exec vitest run src/utils/import-runner-reference-master-scope.test.ts`; expect 10 passed.
- What you need to do: this PR touches `skills/**` (Tier H), so it lands by the maintainer's approval and merge.

## What changes

- **Scope sources** (`referenceScopeSources`, `packages/core/src/utils/import-coerce.ts`). For a reference column of the row, the scope is built from (1) the field's own `dependsOn` (string form: same name on both sides; `{ field, param }`: target field `param`) when the row fills the sibling, and (2) each `master_detail` field the lookup TARGET declares, when exactly one other single-value reference column of the row points at that master object and is filled. Two such columns (bill-to / ship-to) do not say which is the master, so neither scopes.
- **Ordering** (`coerceRow`). Unscoped columns coerce first in row order; a scoped column coerces after its source columns, with their coerced ids as its scope. A failed or non-scalar source scopes nothing. When no pending column is ready (a cycle, or a column whose source waits behind one), every pending column resolves unscoped, as on `main`. Errors are still reported in the row's column order. An optional `sourceRow` lets the match-key pass (`rowsSharingKey`) read the scope from the whole row, so a key column naming a detail groups by the same id the row's own pass resolves, for one level of master: a source column outside the key columns is coerced unscoped, so in a chain (account → contract → milestone) the two passes can differ.
- **Resolver** (`import-runner.ts`). The scope is merged into every candidate's `where` (`{ [candidate]: display, ...scope }`), so a tie and a miss are judged inside it; the cache key carries the scope; a candidate the scope already fixes is skipped. The read is the same `findData` with the same caller `context` as before, so RLS is unchanged and a record the caller cannot read never matches. FLS is not unchanged: the scope puts the target's master field (or a `dependsOn` `param`) into the caller's own `where`, plugin-security's predicate guard refuses a caller `where` on a field the caller cannot read, and the resolver reads that throw as no match. So a caller who cannot read that field gets `reference_not_found` for a scoped cell that resolved on `main`. It fails closed and discloses nothing; it is declared in the `Clause-②` narrowing, the changeset and the docs (option (b) of review#2's S1), and the unscoped retry (option (a)) is not implemented. The target's masters are read off the same served-target declaration the resolver already reads (`servesReferenceTarget`, now also `masters` via `referenceTargetOf`), so a target the caller cannot serve answers no masters.
- **Field meta** (`import-field-meta.ts`). `ExportFieldMeta.dependsOn` carries the normalised `{ field, param }` pairs; present only when declared.
- **Remedy for a narrowed row** (in the changeset and the docs). A pasted id is scoped too, so a row that means another master's detail has no way through in one import: correct the master cell, or, when the cross-master link is intended, leave the master column out of the import and set it in a second update. For the field-permission case, grant the caller read access to that field, or leave the master column out the same way.
- **Docs.** `content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx` (new subsection under cell coercion, with the field-permission case and the remedy) and the data skill's relationships rule (5 lines under `master_detail`). The docs and changeset say the `dependsOn` scope is the filter the record form's picker applies, and that the `master_detail` inference has no picker counterpart, so for a lookup without `dependsOn` the import is stricter than the form.
- Not touched: `packages/spec/**`, the REST import door (`packages/rest/src/import*.ts` feeds `runImport` unchanged; the premise's "likely code" there was measured and the fix lives entirely in core), no stored-data migration.

## Why

Measured premise on `origin/main` 4bba8b8f02: `runImport`'s resolver queried `where: { [field]: display }` over the whole target for every candidate and returned `ambiguous` on two hits; nothing read the row's other columns. The record picker scopes by `dependsOn` / the master, so the two doors disagreed.

## Tests

New `packages/core/src/utils/import-runner-reference-master-scope.test.ts` (10 cases, fake protocol answering equality over every `where` key):

- acceptance 1: two contracts each with "Advance 30%"; rows naming A and B link `m1` and `m2`; column order does not matter.
- acceptance 2: a row with no (or a blank) master cell is `reference_ambiguous`; a unique name still resolves object-wide.
- acceptance 3: a name absent under the row's master, a name unique object-wide but under another master, and a pasted id of another master's detail are all `reference_not_found`.
- every read carries the caller's context; two master columns stay unscoped; a field's own `dependsOn` scopes a plain lookup; a master cell that fails scopes nothing.
- the match-key pass: two keys under different masters are two keys; a key naming another master's detail answers `reference_not_found` on that row alone (unscoped it would fail both rows as a duplicate key).

Ablations (one-shot, restored, `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`; tests import `src` directly, no dist involved):

- `where: { [f]: display, ...(scope ?? {}) }` → `where: { [f]: display }`: 7 failed | 3 passed (the 3 that stay green are the unscoped cases). Restored: blob == HEAD `f33b0cb042ea`, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- `coerceRow(cells, metaMap, coerceCtx, rows[i])` → without `rows[i]`: 1 failed | 9 passed (the match-key case). Restored likewise.


## Acceptance notes

- `dependsOn` is honoured as the picker reads it (`param` names the target field). A `dependsOn` entry naming a column the row leaves blank scopes nothing.
- Review#2 nit N3 is carried, not fixed here: the scoped and unscoped cache keys share one string space (`obj::display` against `obj::display::[...]`), so a display value that itself ends in a serialized scope could collide within one import and one caller.
- The HotCRM import template text (`packages/rest/src/import-template.ts` `howToFill`) still says a name matching more than one record is refused; it is not wrong for a row without its master and was left as is.

## Verification
